name: Norman, Oklahoma, 3 May 1999 (midday balloon)
line: Moist, unstable air (CAPE about 3000 J/kg) with strong wind shear (22 m/s over 6 km).
note: The balloon launched at 1800 UTC (1 pm local time). The storm is started by a gentle push of rising air, as CM1's updraft nudging does. In a 1 km run the storm grows for about 20 minutes and has rained itself out within about 45 minutes; CM1 r21.1 makes the same storm from this air, with the same life (both measured). At 250 m, on the full 120 km area, a 2-hour run of this card also made a storm, strongest in its first half hour. This day's sounding in an idealized storm, not a reconstruction of that day's storms.

gm1_settings_why: The push of rising air that starts the storm is centred 0.9 km east and 10.5 km south of the centre, the storm-track check's recommended place for this sounding, so the storm keeps the most room to every side. CM1 keeps the nudging's centre in its code (xc_wnudge, yc_wnudge), not the namelist, so this is a GM1 setting.
